policies.title: Belarus ordinary passports: visa exemption
policies.summary: The current MOFA agreement table records Belarus ordinary-passport visa exemption, effective 15 January 2026.
conditions: The MOFA table identifies Belarus ordinary passports as covered; its row does not state a separate ordinary-passport stay period, so none is inferred here.
This is not a work, residence, diplomatic/official-document, border-pass, transit, or admission guarantee; ordinary immigration controls still apply.

policies.title: Listed ordinary passports: 30-day visa exemption
policies.summary: The current MOFA agreement table grants these ordinary passports a 30-day visa-exempt stay.
conditions: The current MOFA table identifies a 30-day stay for the listed ordinary passports. It does not establish a work or residence entitlement.

Entry remains subject to travel-document, port, security, immigration inspection, and other Lao legal requirements. Diplomatic, service, public-affairs, temporary, emergency, and special passports are outside this policy.

policies.title: Myanmar ordinary passports: 14-day visa exemption
policies.summary: The current MOFA agreement table grants Myanmar ordinary passports a 14-day visa-exempt stay.
conditions: The table specifies 14 days for ordinary passports. It does not create a work, residence, special-document, or admission entitlement.
Normal immigration inspection and lawful-entry conditions remain applicable.

policies.title: Luxembourg and Swiss ordinary passports: 15-day visa exemption
policies.summary: The current MOFA table lists a 15-day unilateral ordinary-passport exemption for Luxembourg and Switzerland.
conditions: The table labels these unilateral ordinary-passport exemptions at 15 days. It does not establish employment, residence, special-document, or transit rights.
Admission, security, passport, route, and immigration-inspection requirements still apply.

policies.title: Live official selector: listed ordinary passports' tourist eVisa
policies.summary: The current Lao eVisa selector includes these non-exempt ordinary-passport nationalities for the online tourist eVisa route.
conditions: The portal blocks selection of its 15 is_except records; they are the older subset of the current MOFA table's ordinary-passport waiver cohort. The three later MOFA waiver codes Belarus, DPR Korea, and Timor-Leste remain visa-free rather than eVisa.

The selector's stay_day field is not used to set waiver terms: for example, its blocked Japan record says 15 while the current MOFA waiver table says 30. The MOFA table controls the exemption policy and duration.

India and Nepal are selector records with watchlist YES. The application code displays a watchlist acknowledgement; neither the endpoint nor the terms publishes a distinct nationality-wide visa outcome, so this policy does not infer one.

Only ordinary passports qualify: temporary, emergency, special, and other passport types do not. The Tourist Visa T-B3 grants 30 days after arrival and the eVisa is valid 60 days after approval; the cited tourist-eVisa material does not establish work, residence, official/diplomatic, border-pass, or transit routes.

Apply online, pay the non-refundable fee, and carry the approval letter. Use only the nine designated eVisa ports; approval does not ensure admission and immigration may refuse for insufficient funds, criminality, prior deportation, prostitution, drug, or terrorist grounds.

application.label: Lao Official Online Visa
application.processingTime: Usually three working days after completed application and fee; may take longer.
steps: Select an eligible ordinary passport and complete the online tourist eVisa application.
Upload the required photo and passport bio page, then pay the non-refundable fee.
Download and print the approval letter; present it with the same passport at an eVisa-designated port.
